chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu al-Maghra', from Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man whose death approaches, so he sends for his neighbor and marries him his daughter for one thousand dirhams. Is his marriage valid? He said: Yes.

So it does not contradict the first narration, because the meaning in this report is that we assume he consummated the marriage with her, because if that were the case, the contract would be valid as detailed in the first report.
And if he did not consummate the marriage with her and then died, the contract would be invalid.
ai.seo_question: Is a marriage contract valid for a dying man who marries off his daughter?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying the validity of a marriage contract for a man nearing death, resolving an apparent contradiction by specifying that the contract is valid if consummated (*dakhala biha*) but invalid if he dies before consummation. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle that the completion of the essential conditions of marriage, particularly physical union, determines the finality of the bond in cases of imminent death.
